### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **32** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD (literal, a string literal in UNREGISTERED_CODE_SITES; a string literal in lockedAccountRefusal))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/audit-service.mdx`  _(via ACCOUNT_LOCKED (literal, a string literal in admitSignInAttempt; a string literal in lockedAccountRefusal; a string literal in refuseLockedAccountSession), INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD (literal, a string literal in UNREGISTERED_CODE_SITES; a string literal in lockedAccountRefusal), locked_until (literal, a string literal in LOCKED_ACCOUNT_ROW_FIELDS; a string literal in settleSignInAttempt))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD (literal, a string literal in UNREGISTERED_CODE_SITES; a string literal in lockedAccountRefusal))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (literal, 55 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **43** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json aab8b3188a9c7804d6f5164141576c1b856de082` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3348a16451e71601e5190ffa28dc99738ef5f0ca` — the merge of head `4d27b2c90137d087fa2a1abc0f546a74b141645a` into base `aab8b3188a9c7804d6f5164141576c1b856de082`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3348a16451e71601e5190ffa28dc99738ef5f0ca && git checkout 3348a16451e71601e5190ffa28dc99738ef5f0ca
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin aab8b3188a9c7804d6f5164141576c1b856de082 4d27b2c90137d087fa2a1abc0f546a74b141645a && git checkout -B drift-repro aab8b3188a9c7804d6f5164141576c1b856de082 && git merge --no-ff 4d27b2c90137d087fa2a1abc0f546a74b141645a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json aab8b3188a9c7804d6f5164141576c1b856de082
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs aab8b3188a9c7804d6f5164141576c1b856de082` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6617ff70f2334e704b5df6b1c600261223cc4c6e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/plugin-auth-locked-account-every-sign-in-door.md, content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-after-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-database-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-sign-in-lockout.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/locked-account-every-sign-in-door.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sign-in-lockout-refusal.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts + none

Read at 2026-11-15T21:49Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6901766329; lane request 6901751579 on mailbox #33873. Independence: implemented and dispatched by security#1 (sunhaolin); reviewed by os-tesla.

This record stays at the rule layer on purpose (public repository, account lockout). Anything that would describe how a rule could be missed is in the seat's private notes and is not repeated here.

### ① Derived judgments

Read, not run: the diff against merge base `f81e4b6c`, the head tree by `git show`, the PR body and comments, the head's check-runs, and the vendor at the version the lockfile pins (better-auth, `@better-auth/core`, `@better-auth/sso`, `@better-auth/oauth-provider`, `@better-auth/scim`, all 1.7.12; lockfile and `plugin-auth/package.json` agree).

The rule under review: while an account's lock holds, every door that ends in a session for it refuses it with the answer password sign-in gives under `lockoutRefusal`; every password door counts toward the one lock and checks it before the password.

- **One write, one check.** Every vendor path that makes a session goes through the one internal session-creation call, and that call hands `session.create.before` the endpoint context of the request it serves. plugin-auth has three session-creating sites of its own (impersonation, the impersonating administrator's rotation, the principal mint); all three use the same call. The oauth-provider and scim packages create no session. So composing the refusal into `session.create.before` is the right seam, and it sits after the row read that already refuses on a read fault.
- **Door census.** Reached by the new check and refused for a locked account: SMS one-time code, emailed sign-in link (both lanes), verification link that signs in, address-change confirmation opened without a session, every second-factor verify route, social and generic-OAuth callbacks and the id-token sign-in, enterprise SSO callbacks (OIDC and SAML), the device grant. Left to the password gate: email and password, phone number and password. Never a locked account: sign-up. Not a new session: session refresh, the one-time-token handoff of an existing session. Not mounted in this package: username, passkey, email-OTP, anonymous, SIWE, one-tap, multi-session, API-key plugins.
- **Exemptions.** Impersonation: the mark is written only by the two administrator-gated sites; no door copies caller input into it. Own session: the comparison is against the session the request resolved, and only for the same account; a caller with no session cannot reach it. Whether all three are scoped tightly enough is graded in S1 and N1.
- **The answer.** `lockedAccountRefusal` is the single constructor for both settings; `'explicit'` is the same status, code and sentence the gate throws, `'uniform'` is built from the vendor's own constant. At a code or link door the refusal is only ever given after the door's own credential passed, so a caller without a valid credential gets that door's ordinary answer whether or not the account is locked: no account-existence or lock-state answer is added beyond what password sign-in already gives a holder of the correct password. At redirect doors the same code rides the door's error redirect.
- **Phone and password against email and password.** Same reservation, same compare-and-set counter, same lock stamp, same reset on success, same verifier wrapper for the uniform refusal (the vendor's phone door verifies through the wrapped verifier), gate before the vendor's credential check. The account lookup is an exact match on the column the vendor matches. The early `return` added to the before-hook for the phone path skips nothing that applied to it. Session controls and last-login stamp remain email-only, as declared.
- **Newly refused beyond locked accounts.** None found: the check returns unless `lockoutThreshold` is on and the stored lock is still ahead; an expired lock and a deployment with the lockout off are untouched.
- **Head does not compile.** See M1.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are present, line-initial, in both the PR body and the changeset; `fix(plugin-auth)!:` carrier, a **BREAKING** paragraph, and one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, which fits: nothing an author can write is removed or renamed, so there is no FROM to TO mapping to carry. `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/runtime` is the level AGENTS.md prescribes for a non-protocol breaking change. The remedy is stated (the Unlock action). The declaration is under-stated in who moves: S3.

CI on this head (61 check-runs): 32 success, 21 skipped, **2 failure** (`Type Check · workspace`, and `TypeScript Type Check` which reports that lane), 1 cancelled (`Check Changeset`, superseded by a newer run of the same automation, so its verdict on the changeset is not in hand), 5 in progress (`Test Core` shards 2, 3, 5, 7 and 8 of 8). This is a FAIL, so there is nothing for the seat to wait on; the next head needs a full green read including `Check Changeset`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No `packages/spec` change, no schema, no governed path in the diff. ADR-0069 is cited, not edited; its D2 seam cell still names only `/sign-in/email`. The published docs on `main` already say a lock refuses every sign-in that resolves to the account, so the narrowing makes a published refusal real and takes no declared capability away.
- The rule as worded is about new sessions. Live sessions, OAuth tokens and API keys of a locked account are outside it and unchanged; ADR-0069's seam list names locked-account rejection on the session-validation path, which nothing here rules on.
- `packages/runtime` is moved only by a ledger row; that row is what breaks the build (M1).
- The PR body's local readings were taken for plugin-auth at the commit before the last one, and the last commit is the one that reds the runtime type check.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing holds against the published rule, by construction rather than by a list of doors, and the choice to keep password doors on their own gate is what preserves each door's own wrong-password answer under `'uniform'`. The pins are real requests through `handleRequest` with a measured reference answer and controls for each exemption, an unlocked account, an expired lock and the lockout off.

M1 (must-fix) — the head does not type-check. `packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-error-vocabulary.ts:552` writes `shape: 'apierrorarg'`, and `CodeStampShape` in the same file has no such member; CI says exactly that (`Type '"apierrorarg"' is not assignable to type 'CodeStampShape'`, `packages/runtime` typecheck exit 2), and the tree agrees. It is the only row in the table with that shape.

S1 (should-fix) — the rule is not kept on every door that ends in a session in every configuration this repo supports: one of the three exemptions is not scoped tightly enough, and where it is uncertain it degrades toward admitting rather than refusing. Detail is in the seat's notes.

S2 (should-fix) — on the two password doors the rule is held by the gate alone. Gate and session-creation check are two rules that agree today rather than one rule. Tie the session-creation check's treatment of those doors to the gate's recorded verdict for that account. Detail is in the seat's notes.

S3 (should-fix) — the declaration under-states who moves. The tree also refuses a locked account at external-identity sign-in (social, generic OAuth, enterprise SSO), at the device grant and at an address-change confirmation opened without a session; the changeset's **Now** and **Who moves** name none of them, and say nothing of accounts that have no password, which the lock now reaches on doors that never took one. None of those doors has a pin; the second-factor OTP route shares the pinned code path but is not itself pinned. Name the populations in the changeset and the docs sentence, and add a pin with its control for at least one external-identity door and the device grant.

S4 (should-fix) — `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/audit-service.mdx` states when a `login_failed` row is written (a password sign-in that named an account, or an IP allow-list refusal). This diff writes that row, with the lock as its reason, at code, link, second-factor and external-identity doors too. The docs-drift check listed the page; it is untouched.

N1 (nit) — one exemption reads the request's own view of the caller's session rather than the session of record, and the two can differ. Detail is in the seat's notes.

N2 (nit) — the backup-code pin's ablation is declared NOT MEASURED; take it with the next head.

Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qibxTeW8xHnxoHxWNHWW`

Read at 2026-11-15T23:12Z. Delta review of this head against FAIL 6901922014 at 6617ff70; claim: comment 6902833532; taken on patrol as owed. Independence: implemented and dispatched by security#1 (sunhaolin); reviewed by os-tesla.

This record stays at the rule layer on purpose (public repository, account lockout). Anything that would describe how a rule could be missed is in the seat's private notes and is not repeated here.

### ① Derived judgments

Read, not run: the delta `6617ff70..4eadd3d0` (commits `49d4fbb4` and `4eadd3d0`), the whole diff against merge base `f81e4b6c`, the head tree by `git show`, the PR body and comments, the head's check-runs, and the vendor at the pinned version (better-auth, `@better-auth/core`, `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12).

The rule under review is unchanged: while an account's lock holds, every door that ends in a session for it refuses it with the answer password sign-in gives under `lockoutRefusal`; every password door counts toward the one lock and checks it before the password.

The prior record's findings, by id:

- M1: closed.
  The ledger row's shape is a member of `CodeStampShape`, the stamp in `sign-in-lockout-refusal.ts` is written in that shape, and both type-check lanes are green on this head.
- S1: closed.
  Each of the three exemptions now holds only when its own condition is positively established, and a condition that cannot be established is judged a sign-in. That is true in every supported configuration I could read. The correction over-reaches in one of them: see S5.
- S2: closed.
  At a password door the session-creation check admits only on that door's gate verdict `admitted`, recorded in this request for this account and this identifier, and refuses when the verdict is absent. The two rules are now one. Pinned both ways: a request with no verdict recorded gets no session under either setting, with its unlocked control; and the existing cases that sign in with the correct password on the attempt that reaches the threshold hold the admitted branch. By read, each goes red if its branch is removed.
- S3: closed.
  The changeset's Now and Who moves, and the docs sentence, name every door the tree reaches: one-time code, sign-in link, verification link, address-change confirmation opened without a session, the three second-factor routes, identity-provider sign-in (social, generic OAuth, ID token, enterprise SSO), the device grant and the phone-number password door, and they say the lock reaches an account that has no password. The remedy is stated (Unlock). Pins with controls were added for the device grant, an identity-provider callback and the second-factor OTP route. What is still unpinned is N3; what the PR body still says is N4.
- S4: closed.
  `audit-service.mdx` now states that a `login_failed` row is also written, with the lock as its reason, at every other door that ends in a session, and that the password doors are email and phone number.
- N1: closed.
  The own-session exemption is decided from the stored session row the request's token names, read before the endpoint runs and required to be unexpired; the request's own view of its session is no longer consulted. A unit pin holds that, and by read it goes red on reverting.
- N2: open, unchanged.
  The body still declares the backup-code pin's ablation NOT MEASURED. Carried in N4.

New on this head:

- **Newly refused beyond locked accounts.** Outside S5, none found: the session-creation check returns before any new logic unless `lockoutThreshold` is on and the stored lock is still ahead, the new before-hook read never throws and records nothing on a fault, and an unlocked account, an expired lock and a deployment with the lockout off are untouched (controls for each stand). In one supported configuration there is one: S5.
- **Exemption controls.** Impersonation of a locked account, a locked administrator's own rotation, a locked signed-in account's password change that ends its other sessions, and the in-process principal session are each still exercised through a real request and still pass by read, now on the stored session of record.
- **The uniform answer.** `lockedAccountRefusal` builds the vendor's code and sentence as an object literal; the pins compare status, code and sentence against the measured `/sign-in/email` answer, so a vendor rename turns them red.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are present, line-initial, in both the PR body and the changeset; `fix(plugin-auth)!:` carrier, a **BREAKING** paragraph, one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/runtime`. All as judged before, and the changeset's account of who moves is now complete (S3).

CI on this head, complete: 53 check-runs, 38 success, 15 skipped, none failing, none running. `Type Check · workspace`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Check Changeset` are all success. Nothing for the seat to wait on from CI.

### ③ Boundary flags

- No `packages/spec` change, no schema, no governed path in the diff. `packages/runtime` is moved only by the one ledger row.
- While the lockout is on, every auth request that presents a session token now pays one more read of its session row, before the endpoint runs. With the lockout off nothing is read.
- The lock is placed by refused password attempts and now holds at doors that never took a password, for accounts that have none. That is declared in the changeset and the docs. Whether an account with no password should be countable at a password door is a security-lane decision this record does not make.
- As before: live sessions, OAuth tokens and API keys of a locked account are outside the rule as worded and unchanged.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing holds against the published rule, and the delta makes it hold by positive evidence rather than by absence: an exemption is something the request proves, and a password door's session follows the one verdict its gate recorded. The docs on `main` already promised the refusal; this makes it real and takes no declared capability away. The pins added are real requests with measured reference answers and a control beside each.

No must-fix.

S5 (should-fix) — continues S1 and S2. In one supported configuration the corrected check cannot see what it needs to tell a password sign-in its gate admitted from any other new session, and it refuses: an account the gate admitted, presenting the correct password, can be refused at session creation, and that refusal is then settled as a refused credential rather than handed back. The same configuration also refuses, for a locked account, the cases the changeset lists as unchanged. This was introduced by `49d4fbb4`; the head before it admitted there. Read from the tree's own notes on that configuration, not measured. The request-scoped record the gate and the new before-hook write is available there, so the check can consult it before refusing; a pin belongs with the fix. Bounded as S1 was, and graded as S1 was; the seat may regrade. Detail is in the seat's notes.

N3 (nit) — continues S3. Three declared doors have no pin of their own: the address-change confirmation opened without a session, the ID-token sign-in, and the enterprise SSO callbacks. All three end in the one write the check is composed into, and the last two share the pinned callback's code path, so the rule holds by construction; a later vendor move would not be caught at those doors.

N4 (nit) — continues N2. The PR body predates `49d4fbb4`: its readings block names `6617ff70` and 44 cases, the backup-code ablation is still NOT MEASURED, no ablation reading is given for any pin added since, its quick-read lists fewer doors than the changeset, and its account of the exemptions and of the password doors is the previous head's. By read each new pin goes red when its branch is removed; the body should say so from a measurement, and describe this head.

N5 (nit) — where a password door's session is refused at session creation rather than by its gate, the answer and the reason its `login_failed` row records are the general ones and not, in every case, that door's own. Detail is in the seat's notes.

N6 (nit) — the read of the session of record chooses among presented credentials in an order of its own, which is not the vendor's in every case. Where they differ the exemption is not established, so it fails closed. Detail is in the seat's notes.

N7 (nit) — `auth-manager-sign-in-lockout.ts` spells a route constant that a sibling module already exports; import it so the two cannot part.
